requirement: The review prompt MUST direct the reviewer never to rename or move a committed requirement, and to raise a wrong name as a design question instead. When the reviewer splits a committed requirement, the prompt MUST direct it to keep the requirement's full name on the core obligation, to name the parts `<name>.<part>`, and to list every new name.
rationale:
The requirement has two parts. First, the prompt must tell the reviewer never to rename or move a committed requirement, and to raise a wrong name as a design question. Second, when the reviewer splits a committed requirement, the prompt must say three things: keep the full name on the core obligation, name the parts `<name>.<part>`, and list every new name.

The single marked test is `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_review_prompt_never_renames_and_names_split_parts]`. It takes the review prompt text between the "**Mechanical changes:**" and "**Design questions:**" markers. It does this through `review_prompt_between`, which reads the skill file `references/review-prompt.md` and collapses its whitespace. It then uses `assert_text` to assert that the text contains three phrases:
- "Never rename or move a committed requirement; if its name is wrong, raise it as a design question". This covers the never-rename-or-move clause and the raise-as-a-design-question clause.
- "When you split one, keep its full name on the core obligation and name the parts `<name>.<part>`". This covers keeping the full name on the core obligation and the `<name>.<part>` naming.
- "List every new name". This covers listing the new names.

`assert_text` panics with a message if any phrase is missing. `review_prompt_between` panics if either marker is missing. So the assertions do enforce each obligation, and each obligation maps to a concrete assertion.

The requirement concerns the prompt's wording. Checking that the prompt contains these directives is the appropriate test, and the requirement names no other modes, boundaries or failure cases. I found no gap.
